1: //! Verified snapshot integrity with dual-hash scheme.
2: //!
3: //! Models the dual-hash integrity check for Raft snapshots: data and
4: //! metadata are hashed independently, then combined into a single hash.
5: //! Verification recomputes the combined hash and compares. An optional
6: //! chain hash check ties the snapshot to a position in the log's hash
7: //! chain.
8: //!
9: //! Blake3 is modeled as an uninterpreted function (same pattern as
10: //! `chain.rs`) with a trusted collision-resistance axiom and runtime bridge;
11: //! determinism for equal inputs follows from pure spec equality.
12: //!
13: //! Proves: compute→verify round-trip, tamper detection on data and
14: //! metadata independently, chain hash mismatch detection, and the
15: //! combined hash commits to both components.
16: 
17: use vstd::prelude::*;
18: 
19: verus! {
20: 
21: /// Snapshot integrity record.
22: pub struct SnapshotIntegrity {
23:     /// Hash of the snapshot data.
24:     pub data_hash: u64,
25:     /// Hash of the snapshot metadata.
26:     pub meta_hash: u64,
27:     /// Combined hash of `data_hash` and `meta_hash`.
28:     pub combined_hash: u64,
29:     /// Chain hash at the snapshot's log position.
30:     pub chain_hash_at_snapshot: u64,
31: }
32: 
33: // --- Hash function (axiomatized) ---
34: 
35: /// Abstract hash combining two u64 values.
36: ///
37: /// In practice this is blake3(a || b). Modeled as uninterpreted with
38: /// collision resistance kept as an explicit axiom below.
39: // r[depends snapshot-integrity.compute]
40: pub uninterp spec fn dual_hash_spec(a: u64, b: u64) -> u64;
41: 
42: /// Pure spec determinism for equal dual-hash inputs.
43: pub proof fn dual_hash_deterministic(a1: u64, b1: u64, a2: u64, b2: u64)
44:     requires a1 == a2, b1 == b2
45:     ensures dual_hash_spec(a1, b1) == dual_hash_spec(a2, b2)
46: {
47: }
48: 
49: /// Axiom: collision resistance — different inputs produce different outputs.
50: ///
51: /// This is the standard cryptographic assumption. In practice, Blake3's
52: /// 256-bit output makes collisions computationally infeasible.
53: /// @verified-logic:permanent-axiom — cryptographic collision resistance
54: #[verifier::external_body]
55: pub proof fn dual_hash_collision_resistant(a1: u64, b1: u64, a2: u64, b2: u64)
56:     requires dual_hash_spec(a1, b1) == dual_hash_spec(a2, b2)
57:     ensures a1 == a2 && b1 == b2
58: {}
59: 
60: /// Exec wrapper for the hash function (external body — runtime uses a mix).
61: /// @verified-logic:permanent-axiom — crypto primitive, runtime-only
62: // r[impl snapshot-integrity.compute]
63: #[verifier::external_body]
64: pub fn dual_hash(a: u64, b: u64) -> (result: u64)
65:     ensures result == dual_hash_spec(a, b)
66: {
67:     let mut h = a;
68:     h = h.wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005).wrapping_add(b);
69:     h = h.wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005).wrapping_add(a ^ b);
70:     h
71: }
72: 
73: // --- compute_integrity ---
74: 
75: // r[depends snapshot-integrity.compute]
76: /// Spec: compute the snapshot integrity record.
77: pub open spec fn compute_integrity_spec(
78:     data_hash: u64,
79:     meta_hash: u64,
80:     chain_hash_at_snapshot: u64,
81: ) -> SnapshotIntegrity {
82:     SnapshotIntegrity {
83:         data_hash,
84:         meta_hash,
85:         combined_hash: dual_hash_spec(data_hash, meta_hash),
86:         chain_hash_at_snapshot,
87:     }
88: }
89: 
90: // r[impl snapshot-integrity.compute]
91: /// Compute a snapshot integrity record.
92: pub fn compute_integrity(
93:     data_hash: u64,
94:     meta_hash: u64,
95:     chain_hash_at_snapshot: u64,
96: ) -> (result: SnapshotIntegrity)
97:     ensures
98:         result.data_hash == compute_integrity_spec(data_hash, meta_hash, chain_hash_at_snapshot).data_hash,
99:         result.meta_hash == compute_integrity_spec(data_hash, meta_hash, chain_hash_at_snapshot).meta_hash,
100:         result.combined_hash == compute_integrity_spec(data_hash, meta_hash, chain_hash_at_snapshot).combined_hash,
101:         result.chain_hash_at_snapshot == compute_integrity_spec(data_hash, meta_hash, chain_hash_at_snapshot).chain_hash_at_snapshot,
102: {
103:     SnapshotIntegrity {
104:         data_hash,
105:         meta_hash,
106:         combined_hash: dual_hash(data_hash, meta_hash),
107:         chain_hash_at_snapshot,
108:     }
109: }
110: 
111: // --- verify_integrity ---
112: 
113: // r[depends snapshot-integrity.verify]
114: /// Spec: verify snapshot integrity by recomputing the combined hash.
115: pub open spec fn verify_integrity_spec(integrity: SnapshotIntegrity) -> bool {
116:     dual_hash_spec(integrity.data_hash, integrity.meta_hash) == integrity.combined_hash
117: }
118: 
119: // r[impl snapshot-integrity.verify]
120: /// Verify a snapshot integrity record.
121: pub fn verify_integrity(integrity: &SnapshotIntegrity) -> (result: bool)
122:     ensures result == verify_integrity_spec(*integrity)
123: {
124:     dual_hash(integrity.data_hash, integrity.meta_hash) == integrity.combined_hash
125: }
126: 
127: // --- verify_with_chain_hash ---
128: 
129: // r[depends snapshot-integrity.verify-with-chain-hash]
130: /// Spec: verify integrity AND check the chain hash matches.
131: pub open spec fn verify_with_chain_hash_spec(
132:     integrity: SnapshotIntegrity,
133:     expected_chain_hash: u64,
134: ) -> bool {
135:     verify_integrity_spec(integrity)
136:         && integrity.chain_hash_at_snapshot == expected_chain_hash
137: }
138: 
139: // r[impl snapshot-integrity.verify-with-chain-hash]
140: /// Verify integrity with chain hash check.
141: pub fn verify_with_chain_hash(
142:     integrity: &SnapshotIntegrity,
143:     expected_chain_hash: u64,
144: ) -> (result: bool)
145:     ensures result == verify_with_chain_hash_spec(*integrity, expected_chain_hash)
146: {
147:     verify_integrity(integrity) && integrity.chain_hash_at_snapshot == expected_chain_hash
148: }
149: 
150: // --- Safety proofs ---
151: 
152: // r[impl snapshot-integrity.round-trip]
153: // r[verify snapshot-integrity.round-trip]
154: /// Compute then verify always succeeds.
155: proof fn round_trip(data_hash: u64, meta_hash: u64, chain_hash: u64)
156:     ensures verify_integrity_spec(compute_integrity_spec(data_hash, meta_hash, chain_hash))
157: {
158:     dual_hash_deterministic(data_hash, meta_hash, data_hash, meta_hash);
159: }
160: 
161: // r[impl snapshot-integrity.data-tamper-detected]
162: // r[verify snapshot-integrity.data-tamper-detected]
163: /// Changing data_hash breaks verification (via collision resistance).
164: proof fn data_tamper_detected(
165:     data_hash: u64,
166:     meta_hash: u64,
167:     chain_hash: u64,
168:     tampered_data_hash: u64,
169: )
170:     requires tampered_data_hash != data_hash
171:     ensures
172:         !verify_integrity_spec(SnapshotIntegrity {
173:             data_hash: tampered_data_hash,
174:             meta_hash,
175:             combined_hash: compute_integrity_spec(data_hash, meta_hash, chain_hash).combined_hash,
176:             chain_hash_at_snapshot: chain_hash,
177:         })
178: {
179:     let original_combined = dual_hash_spec(data_hash, meta_hash);
180:     let recomputed = dual_hash_spec(tampered_data_hash, meta_hash);
181:     // By collision resistance, if the hashes were equal,
182:     // then tampered_data_hash == data_hash — contradiction.
183:     if recomputed == original_combined {
184:         dual_hash_collision_resistant(tampered_data_hash, meta_hash, data_hash, meta_hash);
185:     }
186: }
187: 
188: // r[impl snapshot-integrity.meta-tamper-detected]
189: // r[verify snapshot-integrity.meta-tamper-detected]
190: /// Changing meta_hash breaks verification (via collision resistance).
191: proof fn meta_tamper_detected(
192:     data_hash: u64,
193:     meta_hash: u64,
194:     chain_hash: u64,
195:     tampered_meta_hash: u64,
196: )
197:     requires tampered_meta_hash != meta_hash
198:     ensures
199:         !verify_integrity_spec(SnapshotIntegrity {
200:             data_hash,
201:             meta_hash: tampered_meta_hash,
202:             combined_hash: compute_integrity_spec(data_hash, meta_hash, chain_hash).combined_hash,
203:             chain_hash_at_snapshot: chain_hash,
204:         })
205: {
206:     let original_combined = dual_hash_spec(data_hash, meta_hash);
207:     let recomputed = dual_hash_spec(data_hash, tampered_meta_hash);
208:     if recomputed == original_combined {
209:         dual_hash_collision_resistant(data_hash, tampered_meta_hash, data_hash, meta_hash);
210:     }
211: }

214: // r[verify snapshot-integrity.chain-hash-mismatch-detected]

1: //! Verified serialization injectivity for canonical byte encodings.
2: //!
3: //! Proves that canonical byte encodings are injective: equal byte
4: //! sequences imply equal input values. Composes with collision-resistance
5: //! axioms from `chain.rs` and `snapshot_integrity.rs` to give the full
6: //! guarantee: same hash → same structure.
7: //!
8: //! All encode functions operate at the `Seq<u8>` spec level. Exec
9: //! wrappers exist for proptest coverage.
10: 
11: use vstd::prelude::*;
12: 
13: verus! {
14: 
15: // ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
16: // u64 little-endian encoding
17: // ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
18: 
19: // r[depends serialize-inj.encode-u64]
20: /// Spec: encode a u64 as 8 bytes, little-endian.
21: ///
22: /// Byte i holds bits [8i, 8i+8) of the value.
23: pub open spec fn encode_u64_spec(v: u64) -> Seq<u8> {
24:     seq![
25:         (v & 0xff) as u8,
26:         ((v >> 8u64) & 0xff) as u8,
27:         ((v >> 16u64) & 0xff) as u8,
28:         ((v >> 24u64) & 0xff) as u8,
29:         ((v >> 32u64) & 0xff) as u8,
30:         ((v >> 40u64) & 0xff) as u8,
31:         ((v >> 48u64) & 0xff) as u8,
32:         ((v >> 56u64) & 0xff) as u8,
33:     ]
34: }
35: 
36: // r[depends serialize-inj.decode-u64]
37: /// Spec: decode a u64 from 8 bytes, little-endian.
38: pub open spec fn decode_u64_spec(bs: Seq<u8>) -> u64
39:     recommends bs.len() == 8
40: {
41:     (bs[0] as u64)
42:         | ((bs[1] as u64) << 8u64)
43:         | ((bs[2] as u64) << 16u64)
44:         | ((bs[3] as u64) << 24u64)
45:         | ((bs[4] as u64) << 32u64)
46:         | ((bs[5] as u64) << 40u64)
47:         | ((bs[6] as u64) << 48u64)
48:         | ((bs[7] as u64) << 56u64)
49: }
50: 
51: // r[impl serialize-inj.encode-u64-length]
52: // r[verify serialize-inj.encode-u64-length]
53: /// Proof: encode_u64 always produces exactly 8 bytes.
54: pub proof fn encode_u64_len(v: u64)
55:     ensures encode_u64_spec(v).len() == 8
56: {}
57: 
58: // r[verify serialize-inj.decode-u64]
59: /// Proof: decode(encode(v)) == v for all u64 values.
60: proof fn encode_u64_roundtrip(v: u64)
61:     ensures decode_u64_spec(encode_u64_spec(v)) == v
62: {
63:     let bs = encode_u64_spec(v);
64:     // Extract bytes into locals — by(bit_vector) can't handle Seq::index
65:     let b0: u8 = bs[0int];
66:     let b1: u8 = bs[1int];
67:     let b2: u8 = bs[2int];
68:     let b3: u8 = bs[3int];
69:     let b4: u8 = bs[4int];
70:     let b5: u8 = bs[5int];
71:     let b6: u8 = bs[6int];
72:     let b7: u8 = bs[7int];
73:     assert(
74:         (b0 as u64)
75:         | ((b1 as u64) << 8u64)
76:         | ((b2 as u64) << 16u64)
77:         | ((b3 as u64) << 24u64)
78:         | ((b4 as u64) << 32u64)
79:         | ((b5 as u64) << 40u64)
80:         | ((b6 as u64) << 48u64)
81:         | ((b7 as u64) << 56u64)
82:         == v
83:     ) by(bit_vector)
84:         requires
85:             b0 == (v & 0xff) as u8,
86:             b1 == ((v >> 8u64) & 0xff) as u8,
87:             b2 == ((v >> 16u64) & 0xff) as u8,
88:             b3 == ((v >> 24u64) & 0xff) as u8,
89:             b4 == ((v >> 32u64) & 0xff) as u8,
90:             b5 == ((v >> 40u64) & 0xff) as u8,
91:             b6 == ((v >> 48u64) & 0xff) as u8,
92:             b7 == ((v >> 56u64) & 0xff) as u8,
93:     ;
94: }

96: // r[verify serialize-inj.encode-u64]
97: /// Proof: encode_u64 is injective — equal byte sequences imply equal values.
98: proof fn encode_u64_injective(a: u64, b: u64)
99:     requires encode_u64_spec(a) == encode_u64_spec(b)
100:     ensures a == b
101: {
102:     encode_u64_roundtrip(a);
103:     encode_u64_roundtrip(b);
104:     // decode(encode(a)) == a, decode(encode(b)) == b
105:     // encode(a) == encode(b) → decode(encode(a)) == decode(encode(b)) → a == b
106: }

108: // r[impl serialize-inj.encode-u64]
109: /// Exec: encode a u64 as 8 bytes, little-endian.
110: pub fn encode_u64(v: u64) -> (result: Vec<u8>)
111:     ensures result@ == encode_u64_spec(v)
112: {
113:     let b0 = (v & 0xff) as u8;
114:     let b1 = ((v >> 8u64) & 0xff) as u8;
115:     let b2 = ((v >> 16u64) & 0xff) as u8;
116:     let b3 = ((v >> 24u64) & 0xff) as u8;
117:     let b4 = ((v >> 32u64) & 0xff) as u8;
118:     let b5 = ((v >> 40u64) & 0xff) as u8;
119:     let b6 = ((v >> 48u64) & 0xff) as u8;
120:     let b7 = ((v >> 56u64) & 0xff) as u8;
121:     let result = vec![b0, b1, b2, b3, b4, b5, b6, b7];
122:     proof {
123:         assert(result@ =~= encode_u64_spec(v));
124:     }
125:     result
126: }

130: pub fn decode_u64(bs: &[u8]) -> (result: u64)
131:     requires bs@.len() == 8
132:     ensures result == decode_u64_spec(bs@)

134:     let result =
135:         (bs[0] as u64)
136:         | ((bs[1] as u64) << 8u64)
137:         | ((bs[2] as u64) << 16u64)
138:         | ((bs[3] as u64) << 24u64)
139:         | ((bs[4] as u64) << 32u64)
140:         | ((bs[5] as u64) << 40u64)
141:         | ((bs[6] as u64) << 48u64)

150: // r[depends serialize-inj.encode-tagged]
151: /// Spec: prepend a single tag byte to a payload.
152: pub open spec fn encode_tagged_spec(tag: u8, payload: Seq<u8>) -> Seq<u8> {
153:     seq![tag] + payload
154: }

156: // r[verify serialize-inj.encode-tagged]
157: /// Proof: encode_tagged produces len(payload) + 1 bytes.
158: proof fn encode_tagged_len(tag: u8, payload: Seq<u8>)
159:     ensures encode_tagged_spec(tag, payload).len() == payload.len() + 1

162: // r[impl serialize-inj.tag-disjoint]
163: // r[verify serialize-inj.tag-disjoint]
164: /// Proof: different tags produce different encodings regardless of payload.
165: proof fn tag_disjoint(t1: u8, t2: u8, p1: Seq<u8>, p2: Seq<u8>)
166:     requires t1 != t2
167:     ensures encode_tagged_spec(t1, p1) != encode_tagged_spec(t2, p2)
168: {
169:     let e1 = encode_tagged_spec(t1, p1);
170:     let e2 = encode_tagged_spec(t2, p2);
171:     // First byte of e1 is t1, first byte of e2 is t2.
172:     assert(e1[0int] == t1);
173:     assert(e2[0int] == t2);
174:     // t1 != t2, so e1 != e2.
175: }

177: // r[impl serialize-inj.encode-tagged-injective]
178: // r[verify serialize-inj.encode-tagged-injective]
179: /// Proof: same tag with equal encodings implies equal payloads.
180: proof fn encode_tagged_injective(tag: u8, p1: Seq<u8>, p2: Seq<u8>)
181:     requires encode_tagged_spec(tag, p1) == encode_tagged_spec(tag, p2)
182:     ensures p1 == p2
183: {
184:     let e1 = encode_tagged_spec(tag, p1);
185:     let e2 = encode_tagged_spec(tag, p2);
186:     // e1 == e2, and e1.len() == 1 + p1.len(), e2.len() == 1 + p2.len()
187:     assert(e1.len() == 1 + p1.len());
188:     assert(e2.len() == 1 + p2.len());
189:     // Lengths equal, so p1.len() == p2.len()
190:     // For each i in 0..p1.len(): e1[1+i] == p1[i] and e2[1+i] == p2[i]
191:     assert forall|i: int| 0 <= i < p1.len() implies p1[i] == p2[i] by {
192:         assert(e1[1 + i] == p1[i]);
193:         assert(e2[1 + i] == p2[i]);
194:     }
195:     assert(p1 =~= p2);
196: }

198: // r[impl serialize-inj.encode-tagged]
199: /// Exec: prepend a tag byte to a payload.
200: pub fn encode_tagged(tag: u8, payload: &[u8]) -> (result: Vec<u8>)
201:     requires payload@.len() < usize::MAX as int
202:     ensures result@ == encode_tagged_spec(tag, payload@)
203: {
204:     let mut result = Vec::with_capacity(payload.len() + 1);
205:     result.push(tag);
206:     let mut i: usize = 0;
207:     while i < payload.len()
208:         invariant
209:             0 <= i <= payload.len(),
210:             result@.len() == 1 + i as int,
211:             result@[0int] == tag,
212:             forall|j: int| 0 <= j < i as int ==> result@[j + 1] == payload@[j],
213:         decreases payload.len() - i
214:     {
215:         result.push(payload[i]);
216:         i = i + 1;
217:     }
218:     proof {
219:         assert(result@ =~= encode_tagged_spec(tag, payload@));
220:     }
221:     result
222: }

226: // ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

228: // r[depends serialize-inj.encode-len-prefixed]
229: /// Spec: encode data with an 8-byte LE length prefix.
230: pub open spec fn encode_len_prefixed_spec(data: Seq<u8>) -> Seq<u8>
231:     recommends data.len() <= u64::MAX as int
232: {
233:     encode_u64_spec(data.len() as u64) + data
234: }
235: 
236: // r[verify serialize-inj.encode-len-prefixed]
237: /// Proof: length-prefixed encoding is injective.
238: proof fn encode_len_prefixed_injective(a: Seq<u8>, b: Seq<u8>)
239:     requires
240:         a.len() <= u64::MAX as int,
241:         b.len() <= u64::MAX as int,
242:         encode_len_prefixed_spec(a) == encode_len_prefixed_spec(b),
243:     ensures a == b
244: {
245:     let ea = encode_len_prefixed_spec(a);
246:     let eb = encode_len_prefixed_spec(b);
247:     // ea == eb means encode_u64(a.len()) + a == encode_u64(b.len()) + b.
248:     // First 8 bytes: encode_u64(a.len()) == encode_u64(b.len()).
249:     let la = encode_u64_spec(a.len() as u64);
250:     let lb = encode_u64_spec(b.len() as u64);
251:     assert(la.len() == 8) by { encode_u64_len(a.len() as u64); }
252:     assert(lb.len() == 8) by { encode_u64_len(b.len() as u64); }
253:     // First 8 bytes are equal.
254:     assert(la =~= ea.subrange(0, 8));
255:     assert(lb =~= eb.subrange(0, 8));
256:     assert(la =~= lb);
257:     // Therefore a.len() == b.len().
258:     encode_u64_injective(a.len() as u64, b.len() as u64);
259:     // Remaining bytes: a == b.
260:     assert(a =~= ea.subrange(8, ea.len() as int));
261:     assert(b =~= eb.subrange(8, eb.len() as int));
262:     assert(a =~= b);
263: }
264: 
265: // r[verify serialize-inj.encode-len-prefixed]
266: /// Proof: the first 8 bytes of a length-prefixed encoding decode to data.len().
267: proof fn encode_len_prefixed_length_recovery(data: Seq<u8>)
268:     requires data.len() <= u64::MAX as int
269:     ensures decode_u64_spec(encode_len_prefixed_spec(data).subrange(0, 8)) == data.len() as u64
270: {
271:     let encoded = encode_len_prefixed_spec(data);
272:     let la = encode_u64_spec(data.len() as u64);
273:     encode_u64_len(data.len() as u64);
274:     assert(la =~= encoded.subrange(0, 8));
275:     encode_u64_roundtrip(data.len() as u64);
276: }

278: // r[impl serialize-inj.encode-len-prefixed]
279: /// Exec: encode data with a length prefix.
280: pub fn encode_len_prefixed(data: &[u8]) -> (result: Vec<u8>)
281:     requires data@.len() <= usize::MAX as int - 8
282:     ensures result@ == encode_len_prefixed_spec(data@)
283: {
284:     let len_bytes = encode_u64(data.len() as u64);
285:     let mut result = Vec::with_capacity(8 + data.len());
286:     let mut i: usize = 0;
287:     while i < 8
288:         invariant
289:             0 <= i <= 8,
290:             len_bytes@.len() == 8,
291:             result@.len() == i as int,
292:             forall|j: int| 0 <= j < i as int ==> result@[j] == len_bytes@[j],
293:         decreases 8 - i
294:     {
295:         result.push(len_bytes[i]);
296:         i = i + 1;
297:     }
298:     let mut k: usize = 0;
299:     while k < data.len()
300:         invariant
301:             0 <= k <= data.len(),
302:             data@.len() <= usize::MAX as int - 8,
303:             result@.len() == 8 + k as int,
304:             forall|j: int| 0 <= j < 8 ==> result@[j] == len_bytes@[j],
305:             forall|j: int| 0 <= j < k as int ==> result@[8 + j] == data@[j],
306:         decreases data.len() - k
307:     {
308:         result.push(data[k]);
309:         k = k + 1;
310:     }
311:     proof {
312:         assert(result@ =~= encode_len_prefixed_spec(data@));
313:     }
314:     result
315: }

480: // r[impl serialize-inj.encode-quad]
481: /// Exec: encode four u64 values.
482: pub fn encode_quad(a: u64, b: u64, c: u64, d: u64) -> (result: Vec<u8>)
483:     ensures result@ == encode_quad_spec(a, b, c, d)
484: {
485:     let ea = encode_u64(a);
486:     let eb = encode_u64(b);
487:     let ec = encode_u64(c);
488:     let ed = encode_u64(d);
489:     let mut result = Vec::with_capacity(32);
490:     // Copy all four 8-byte segments
491:     let mut i: usize = 0;
492:     while i < 8
493:         invariant
494:             0 <= i <= 8,
495:             ea@.len() == 8,
496:             result@.len() == i as int,
497:             forall|j: int| 0 <= j < i as int ==> result@[j] == ea@[j],
498:         decreases 8 - i
499:     {
500:         result.push(ea[i]);
501:         i = i + 1;
502:     }
503:     i = 0;
